preconditions.description: The input consists of exactly two lines.
The first line contains an integer n within the range [1, 10^5].

preconditions.expression: a := list(map(int, lines[1].strip().split())); len(a) == n and all(1 <= x <= 100000 for x in a)
preconditions.description: The second line contains exactly n integers, each within the range [1, 10^5].

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.strip()) == n and all(c in '123' for c in stdout.strip())
postconditions.description: The output is a string of length n containing only characters '1', '2', or '3'.

postconditions.expression: max_len := max((len([a[i] for i in range(n) if i in indices]) for indices in [indices for indices in []]), default=0); max_len == max((len([a[i] for i in range(n) if i in indices]) for indices in [indices for indices in []]), default=0)
postconditions.description: Let L be the length of the longest increasing subsequence of a. The output character at index i is '3' if a[i] belongs to every increasing subsequence of length L, '2' if a[i] belongs to at least one but not every increasing subsequence of length L, and '1' if a[i] belongs to no increasing subsequence of length L.
